personnelNumberFormat.notes: Regex ^P-[1-4]-(0[1-8])-\d{4}$. T = tier at the time of issue (1-4); YY = two-digit year of OSC intake (01-08); NNNN = serial within that intake year, issued in sequence from 0001 and never reused. The number is issued once and is not reissued on promotion, transfer or detachment, so T records tier at intake, not current tier. Personnel carried as DETACHED / UNPOSTED keep their number. P-3-06-1147 is reserved for the operator (the visitor) and is not listed in the roster.

anomalies.title: The missing 790
anomalies.canonAnswer: Tier totals (3,847) count every person on the OSC payroll; facility staff (3,057) count only those posted to a site. The 790 difference is carried as "DETACHED / UNPOSTED", a payroll category no directive defines. It appears in personnel totals with no drill-down.

anomalies.title: 847 miles versus engineering length
anomalies.canonAnswer: 847 miles is the certified figure reported to the Council. Engineering tables give rail 6,074 miles (sum of six segments) and tram 10,538 miles (sum of four network totals, equal to the sum of the 27 listed links). The Transit app shows engineering figures; the Tier 1 summary shows 847. Neither is corrected.

anomalies.title: Sustained versus surge capacity
anomalies.canonAnswer: 23,400 is SUSTAINED CAPACITY: persons the network can keep alive at full reserves. 34,700 is SURGE BERTHING: the sum of every class's stated capacity. Utilization (16.4%) and phase targets use 23,400; facility pages use their own berthing figures.

anomalies.title: Segment 04 not in revenue service
anomalies.canonAnswer: Segment 04 (ALPHA-02 to ALPHA-05, 891 mi) appears in the segment table but in neither facility's connection list. It was completed March 2007 and is NOT IN REVENUE SERVICE. No reason is recorded.

anomalies.title: No electronic copies permitted
anomalies.canonAnswer: The Facility Inventory is distributed in 11 physical copies with no electronic copies permitted, yet a partially redacted scan of it is held in the Records Library. Records Division has an open security incident on it.

anomalies.title: Meal stocks imply one meal per person per day
anomalies.canonAnswer: 47 million meals for 23,400 persons for 5.5 years works out to 1.0 meal per person per day. At three meals a day the same stock lasts 670 days (1.83 years). The 5.5-year figure stands as the Council figure; the ration basis is not stated anywhere.

anomalies.title: Small-arms reserve arithmetic
anomalies.canonAnswer: "Full capacity + 400% reserve" means five weapons per armed position. 68,000 / 5 = 13,600, which matches neither 23,400 (117,000 needed) nor 34,700 (173,500). The figure stands; the basis for 13,600 is not given.

anomalies.title: Twelve primary hubs
anomalies.canonAnswer: The executive summary says the network connects 12 primary hub installations. Only the five ALPHA sites are called hubs anywhere in the source; twelve is the BETA count. Canon keeps 12 as the certified headline figure without a list behind it.

anomalies.title: Two utilization bases
anomalies.canonAnswer: The 16.4% headline divides tier totals (including the 790 unposted) by sustained capacity. Every facility and class percentage divides posted staff by that site's berthing (surge) figure. On one basis throughout, the network is 8.8% (posted / surge) or 13.1% (posted / sustained).

anomalies.title: Tram links shorter than the straight-line distance
anomalies.canonAnswer: Placed by their stated anchors, 17 of the 27 tram links are shorter than the great-circle distance between their end points (BETA-02 to GAMMA-03 is listed at 97 mi against about 201 mi). Rail segments are all longer than the straight line, as they should be. The listed mileages stand as engineering figures; the geographic view draws links between computed positions and does not label them with length.

anomalies.title: The 7:1 support-to-command ratio
anomalies.canonAnswer: Across the five ALPHA sites, 1,255 non-command staff to 162 command staff is 7.7:1 (sites range 5.8:1 to 9.8:1). Network-wide Tier 3 and 4 to Tier 1 and 2 is 13.9:1, and the full-staffing model (8% command) is 11.5:1. "Approximately 7:1" holds only for ALPHA command lines.
